title: ASP.NET Core Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Make a minimal route
examples.description: MapGet connects a GET path to a function. Open GET /.

examples.title: Return a data object
examples.description: Results.Json sends structured data as JSON. Open GET /book.

examples.title: Read a path input
examples.description: Curly braces name a route value. Open GET /hello/Ravi.

examples.title: Constrain a route number
examples.description: The int route constraint only matches whole numbers. Open GET /double/4.

examples.title: Read an optional query
examples.description: A simple input outside the path can come from the query string. GET /page with no n uses the fallback.

examples.title: Read a JSON record
examples.description: A record can describe body data. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.

examples.title: Check a body value
examples.description: The handler checks a title before returning a created response. Send POST /books with {"title":"Moon Trip"}.

examples.title: Add a shared response rule
examples.description: Middleware can run before and after later handlers. GET /note carries the header set here.

examples.title: Group related paths
examples.description: MapGroup gives several routes one common prefix. Open GET /api/books.

examples.title: Receive a shared helper
examples.description: A registered service can be an input to a handler. Open GET /school.

examples.title: Return a missing-item reply
examples.description: Results.NotFound gives a 404 response. Open GET /missing.

examples.title: Point a client elsewhere
examples.description: Results.Redirect sends a location. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello.
